newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still up sharply with cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still up sharply with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained sharply higher late Tuesday in active trade, still driven by a cash rally that left physical prices more than a dime above the screen, industry sources said.
By 1430 EDT, September surged 11.9 cents to $2.545 per million British thermal units, while October was 10 cents higher at $2.545. Others were up 1.5 to 10.5 cents.

"Weather doesn't mean anything anymore. It's all technical. The funds renewed buying in the front today because of the cash. I think they're trying to retest the highs in the $2.60s (basis September)," said a Texas-based trader.

Most agreed bears were driven to the sidelines recently by concerns about lagging storage and a persistent and growing cash premium to paper. Stocks are almost 10 percent below the three-year average.

"I keep looking for extra gas to show up, but a lot of sellers say they don't have any gas to sell and that's odd for August," said an East Coast trader, adding physical players have been short gas this month despite mild weather.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 62 bcf to 90 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks gained 93 bcf.

Technical traders still pegged September resistance at $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605. Further selling was likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was still seen at Friday's low of $2.395 and then at $2.34 and $2.30. Better buying was expected in the $2.25-2.27 area.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed about a nickel to the high-$2.50s. Midcon pipes were up a couple of cents to mid-$2.40s. New York city gate gas also firmed a few cents to about the $2.80 level.
NYMEX said 53,784 contracts traded by 1355 EDT. Hub open interest on Aug 18 rose 878 contracts to 220,620.
On KCBT, September jumped 11.5 cents to $2.47, while deferreds were steady to 7.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.4 cent to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
